::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** April 27th [1867]  
**Manuscript:** MS Charlotte Mitchell[^1]
:::

My dear <u>[Edith](people/person_749.qmd)</u>
Having always so heard and thought of you it seems the more natural. I was sending a parcel to [Dr Moberly](people/person_1015.qmd)’s, and so put yours with it. Alas - what shall we do when it is Dr Moberly’s no longer-![^2] You will find, shut into the book a paraphrase of some lines in German that [Alexandrine](people/person_1988.qmd) wrote when she sold her pearl necklace - they were written out from the [Month](organizations/other_91.qmd).[^3] I mention it lest you should find the paper astray and be at a loss where it came from.

The [gates of Paradise](other_books/otherbook_483.qmd) are gone to the printer and I shall probably send you a proof in about a fortnight. 

Have you seen the [Copsley Annals](other_books/otherbook_487.qmd), it is a very pretty book that does not seem to be enough known, and it is just the thing for superior village libraries.

yours very sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper. CMY used black-edged paper for all the letters we have found dating from the next two and a half months.
[^2]: George Moberly resigned as headmaster of Winchester College in 1866 but the family’s holiday home, Field House, remained theirs until July 1868.
[^3]: Alexandrine de la Ferronnays, sister-in-law of Pauline Craven; her adventures are described in the latter's *Récit d’une soeur* . In *The Pillars of the House* Mr Audley likens Sister Constance to her.
